opp_008:n1.prompt:
You are helping me draft a company email that must go through an approval gate before sending. Please do NOT send anything yet — this step is only to prepare the draft for my review.

First, ask me for any details you need that aren't already clear, such as: the recipient(s) or recipient list, the sending company email account/address to use, the purpose and key message of the email, desired tone (formal, casual, promotional, etc.), any specific facts, offers, dates, or links to include, and whether there's a template or past email I should match in style.

Once you have this information, draft a complete email including:
- A clear, relevant subject line
- A greeting appropriate to the recipient
- A well-organized body covering the purpose and key points I gave you
- A appropriate sign-off with the company name/sender
- Any necessary disclaimers or links, if relevant

Write the draft in plain text (not sent, not scheduled) and present it to me in full inside your reply, clearly labeled as a DRAFT FOR REVIEW. Include the intended recipient(s) and subject line at the top for context. If any information I gave you seems inconsistent or incomplete (e.g., missing recipient email, unclear call to action), flag it explicitly rather than guessing.

Do not access the company email account to send or schedule the message, and do not take any action beyond producing the draft. This step must stop for human sign-off — I will review the draft and approve, edit, or reject it before any sending happens.

When done, report back with the full draft text, the proposed recipient and subject line, and a short list of any open questions or missing details that need my input before this can be finalized.

opp_008:n2.prompt:
You are helping me draft and send an email from our company account using {{vendor}}, our connected email tool, with a human approval gate before anything is sent. 

First, ask me for anything you don't already have: the recipient(s), subject line, key points or context for the body, desired tone/voice, and whether this should be a new email or a reply to an existing thread/draft. Also confirm that {{vendor}} is already connected to the company account with your configured credentials (scoped, least-privilege access) — if not connected, tell me what needs to be set up and pause.

Once you have the inputs: draft the email in the appropriate voice and tone (professional, matching how our company typically writes), keeping it concise and specific to the context I gave you. Use the {{vendor}} create_and_send_email or send_existing_draft capability to prepare the message as a draft tied to the connected company account — do NOT send it yet. If a relevant draft already exists in the inbox, use send_existing_draft as the target action instead of creating a new one.

Present me with: the full draft (recipient, subject, body), which account it will send from, and which action (create_and_send_email vs send_existing_draft) will be used. Then stop for human sign-off — do not send, submit, or approve the email yourself under any circumstances, even if you believe it's ready. Wait for my explicit approval.

Once I approve, execute the send action and confirm back to me with a timestamp, the recipient(s), and subject line so I have a record the email went out from the company account.

opp_008:n3.prompt:
You are helping me monitor a company email thread for a reply and surface it once it arrives. This is an async, poll-based task: the reply may take hours or days, so you'll need to check back periodically rather than expecting an instant result.

Before starting, ask me for anything you don't already have:
1. Which email account/provider to monitor (e.g., Gmail or Outlook) and confirm you should use my configured credentials to access it.
2. Identifying details of the sent email to watch for a reply to — recipient address, subject line, and approximate send date/time.
3. How often I want you to check (e.g., every few hours, once a day) and for how long before giving up.
4. Where and how I want the reply surfaced — e.g., posted in a specific Slack channel, summarized in a doc, or reported directly back to me in this chat.

Actions to take:
- Locate the original sent email/thread using the details I gave you.
- On each check-in, search the inbox (and relevant folders) for a reply matching that thread (same subject/thread ID or from that recipient).
- When a reply is found, extract the sender, timestamp, and full message body/content.
- Surface it per my stated preference (post, summarize, or report back), including a link or reference to the original thread for context.
- If no reply has arrived by the check, note that briefly and continue polling per the schedule until the reply arrives or the monitoring window I specified ends.

Done looks like: the reply has been found, its content and metadata captured, and it has been surfaced to me in the format and location I requested — or the monitoring window has elapsed with no reply, which you should also report clearly. Report back with the outcome, timestamp of detection, and where you surfaced it.
